sources.quote: Yet while one utility has 15 percent of its customers with rooftop solar, the other has less than 5 percent.
sources.searcher_note: Arizona energy attorney Court Rich compares APS (15%) with SRP (<5%); same article says SRP's solar rates led installations 'to drop by up to 95 percent between 2014 and 2015'. No TEP figure.

sources.quote: Rooftop solar adoption is three times higher in neighboring utility territories.
sources.searcher_note: Advocacy NGO post on SRP's 2025 pricing case; states adoption gap vs neighboring utilities without naming them or giving per-1,000 figures.

sources.quote: In the year immediately prior to implementing the fees, SRP received an average of 600 new rooftop solar applications per month. Today, it receives 25 applications per month
sources.searcher_note: Earliest found: SRP's own spokesman on the post-2015 collapse in rooftop solar applications; speaks to the lead's slow 2014-19 SRP growth.

sources.quote: have decimated what was previously a robust market for solar
sources.searcher_note: Vote Solar's FERC PURPA petition against SRP, as quoted by Utility Dive; SRP says it had more than 54,000 residential rooftop solar customers as of Sept. 30, 2023. Page blocks curl; WebFetch read it.

sources.quote: that number continues to grow at a similar pace to other local utilities.
sources.searcher_note: Disagreement: SRP says its 55,000+ residential solar customers (as of Jan 2023) grow at a similar pace to other local utilities. Opposite direction to the lead's 2014-19 growth comparison.

notes: Several sources name SRP and say its rooftop solar adoption is well below APS / neighboring utilities (Grist 15% vs under 5%; Vote Solar 'three times higher'). None found gives per-1,000-home rates (56.7 / 145.4 / 124.3) or the 2014-19 added-per-1,000 figures, and none names Tucson Electric Power in an adoption comparison. SRP's own blog disputes the direction for recent growth. Also checked, not recorded: Solar United Neighbors AZ net-metering page (no adoption comparison), srpexperience.com campaign site (buyback rates only), KJZZ 2025-07-30 (APS numbers only), Utility Dive 2024-03-25 FERC no-action piece (no adoption numbers).
